quizQuestions.question: Which principle is essential when enforcing database security in a multi-tenant application?
options: Rely entirely on frontend client state checks
Enforce Row Level Security (RLS) policies and server-side role validation
Store all tenant records in separate unauthenticated databases
Grant client browser direct master credentials with no filters
quizQuestions.explanation: Row Level Security (RLS) evaluated on the database server ensures users can never read or write records outside their authorized tenant scope.

quizQuestions.question: In React 19, what is the recommended practice for state management of async server data?
options: Global setInterval loops polling every 100 milliseconds
Caching server data with TanStack Query or native server components with optimistic updates
Storing entire database tables in component local useState hooks
Hardcoding JSON mocks in bundle index.html
quizQuestions.explanation: TanStack Query provides declarative caching, automatic deduplication, background revalidation, and smooth optimistic updates.

quizQuestions.question: Why should user roles never be stored directly in a publicly editable profile table?
options: Because profiles are larger than role tables
To prevent privilege escalation where users update their own profile to claim admin status
Postgres does not allow columns named role
quizQuestions.explanation: Separating roles into a dedicated table protected by admin-only RLS policies prevents malicious users from self-elevating privileges.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary benefit of TypeScript strict mode in full-stack applications?
options: It speeds up internet connection bandwidth
It catches null pointers, unmatched payloads, and type mismatches at compile time
It automatically writes CSS styling rules
It removes the need for database tables
quizQuestions.explanation: Strict mode catches missing fields, undefined handling, and API signature mismatches before code ever runs in production.

quizQuestions.question: When designing idempotent REST APIs, what does an idempotent operation guarantee?
options: The operation can only be called once in the lifetime of the server
Making multiple identical requests has the same intended effect as a single request
The server response will always be an HTTP 500 status code
No data can ever be read by any client
quizQuestions.explanation: Idempotence guarantees that repeated executions (such as network retries) produce the same state change without unintended duplicate records.

quizQuestions.question: Which HTML element is the most semantically correct for the primary navigation links of a page?
quizQuestions.explanation: The <nav> tag is specifically designed in HTML5 to house primary navigation links for accessibility and SEO.

quizQuestions.question: In the CSS box model, what is the layer between the padding and the margin?
quizQuestions.explanation: The CSS box model consists of content, padding, border, and margin from inside to outside.

quizQuestions.question: Which CSS property defines how flex items distribute space along the main axis?
quizQuestions.explanation: justify-content controls alignment and spacing along the main flex axis, whereas align-items controls the cross axis.

quizQuestions.question: What does setting box-sizing: border-box do in modern CSS?
options: Adds a 1px border to all elements
Includes padding and border within the element specified width and height
quizQuestions.explanation: border-box makes layout predictable by including padding and border inside the declared width and height.

quizQuestions.question: In CSS Grid, what does the unit "1fr" represent?
options: One fraction of available remaining grid space
One frame per second for animation
quizQuestions.explanation: The fr unit represents a fraction of the available free space in the grid container.

quizQuestions.question: Which HTML attribute specifies alternative text for images if the image fails to load?
quizQuestions.explanation: The alt attribute provides alternative text essential for accessibility screen readers and search engines.

quizQuestions.question: Which CSS media query targets screens with a viewport width of 768 pixels or wider?
quizQuestions.explanation: Mobile-first design uses @media (min-width: 768px) to apply styles on tablets and larger viewports.

quizQuestions.question: Which CSS display property turns an element into a block-level container that establishes a grid formatting context?
quizQuestions.explanation: display: grid defines the element as a grid container and establishes a new grid formatting context for its direct children.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main difference between let and const in JavaScript?
options: const has function scope while let has block scope
const cannot be reassigned after declaration while let can
let is hoisted to the top while const is not
const only stores objects and arrays
quizQuestions.explanation: Variables declared with const cannot be reassigned, whereas let allows reassignment within its block scope.

quizQuestions.question: What does a closure in JavaScript allow an inner function to access?
options: Variables from its outer enclosing lexical scope even after that outer function has returned
Only global variables declared on window
Private memory allocated by the operating system
quizQuestions.explanation: A closure is the combination of a function bundled together with references to its surrounding state (lexical environment).

quizQuestions.question: Which array method creates a new array populated with the results of calling a provided function on every element?
quizQuestions.explanation: map() returns a new array with transformed elements without mutating the original array.

quizQuestions.question: What does the JavaScript event loop do when the call stack is empty?
options: It powers off the browser engine
It checks the microtask queue first, then dequeues from the callback/task queue
It re-runs the entire script from line 1
quizQuestions.explanation: The event loop processes all pending microtasks (like resolved Promise callbacks) before picking the next macrotask.

quizQuestions.question: What does typeof null return in JavaScript due to a legacy bug?
quizQuestions.explanation: typeof null returns "object", which is a well-known historical JavaScript quirk kept for backwards compatibility.

quizQuestions.question: What state is a JavaScript Promise in initially before it resolves or rejects?
quizQuestions.explanation: A Promise begins in the "pending" state until it is either fulfilled or rejected.

quizQuestions.question: What does event.stopPropagation() do in a DOM event handler?
options: Cancels the default browser action like following a link
Stops the event from bubbling up or capturing down the DOM tree
Prevents the user from clicking the mouse
quizQuestions.explanation: stopPropagation() prevents further propagation of the current event in the capturing and bubbling phases.

quizQuestions.question: How do you correctly convert a JavaScript object into a JSON string?
quizQuestions.explanation: JSON.stringify() serializes a JavaScript object or value into a valid JSON formatted string.

quizQuestions.question: Why should you never mutate state directly in React (e.g., state.count = 5)?
options: Because it throws a fatal compiler error in Vite
Because React relies on shallow reference comparison to detect state changes and trigger re-renders
Because variables in JavaScript are always read-only
Because direct mutation deletes the browser cache
quizQuestions.explanation: React compares previous and new state references; mutating an object directly keeps the reference identical, preventing necessary UI re-renders.

quizQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the dependency array in useEffect(callback, [deps])?
options: It specifies which state or prop changes should re-run the effect
It defines CSS classes for the component
It lists all child components of the effect
quizQuestions.explanation: React only re-runs the effect callback when values in the dependency array change between renders.

quizQuestions.question: What hook should you use to cache an expensive calculation between renders?
quizQuestions.explanation: useMemo caches the result of a computation until its dependencies change.

quizQuestions.question: What is the role of the "key" prop when rendering a dynamic list in React?
options: It is sent to the server for authentication
It helps React identify which items have changed, added, or removed during virtual DOM reconciliation
It automatically styles list items with unique colors
It encrypts the list items on the client
quizQuestions.explanation: Keys give elements a stable identity across renders, allowing React to efficiently update only the changed DOM nodes.

quizQuestions.question: Which hook provides a mutable ref object whose .current property persists across re-renders without triggering a re-render?
quizQuestions.explanation: useRef holds values across renders without causing component re-renders when modified.

quizQuestions.question: What does React Context API solve in large applications?
options: Prop drilling across multiple layers of intermediate components
quizQuestions.explanation: Context allows data to be passed through the component tree without manually passing props down through every level.

quizQuestions.question: When does a cleanup function returned from useEffect execute?
options: Only when the user closes the browser
Before the component unmounts and before re-running the effect on dependency change
quizQuestions.explanation: The cleanup function executes before the component is removed from the DOM and before the effect runs again.

quizQuestions.question: What is the main benefit of code-splitting with React.lazy and Suspense?
options: Reduces initial bundle size by downloading components only when needed
quizQuestions.explanation: React.lazy enables loading bundle chunks on demand, drastically accelerating initial page load times.

quizQuestions.question: What library provides the event loop and asynchronous I/O capabilities in Node.js?
quizQuestions.explanation: Libuv is a multi-platform C library that handles the event loop, thread pool, and asynchronous I/O operations in Node.js.

quizQuestions.question: In Express, what must middleware call to pass control to the next handler in the stack?
quizQuestions.explanation: Middleware functions accept (req, res, next) and must invoke next() to pass execution to the subsequent middleware.

quizQuestions.question: What HTTP status code indicates that the client request lacks valid authentication credentials?
quizQuestions.explanation: 401 Unauthorized signifies that the client must authenticate themselves to get the requested response.

quizQuestions.question: What is the difference between HTTP 401 Unauthorized and HTTP 403 Forbidden?
options: 401 means credentials are bad/missing; 403 means authenticated but lacks permission
401 is for server errors; 403 is for network timeouts
There is no difference in the HTTP specification
quizQuestions.explanation: 401 indicates lack of valid credentials; 403 indicates the server understands who you are but refuses authorization.

quizQuestions.question: Why should passwords NEVER be stored in plain text or MD5 in a database?
options: Plain text takes up too much database disk space
They are easily leaked or cracked with rainbow tables; slow salted hashes like bcrypt are required
Node.js will crash if passwords are plain text
quizQuestions.explanation: bcrypt and Argon2 use cryptographic salts and adaptive work factors to resist brute-force and rainbow table attacks.

quizQuestions.question: What Express middleware package sets sensible HTTP response security headers?
quizQuestions.explanation: Helmet helps secure Express apps by setting various HTTP headers like Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, etc.

quizQuestions.question: What are the three parts of a JSON Web Token (JWT) separated by dots?
quizQuestions.explanation: A JWT consists of three Base64URL-encoded parts: Header (algorithm), Payload (claims), and Signature.

quizQuestions.question: How do you prevent an unhandled asynchronous error from crashing an Express server?
options: Use try/catch inside async route handlers or an async error wrapper that passes errors to next(err)
quizQuestions.explanation: Passing errors to next(err) triggers Express centralized 4-parameter error handling middleware (err, req, res, next).

quizQuestions.question: In MongoDB, what data format is used internally for storage and network transfer?
quizQuestions.explanation: BSON extends JSON with additional data types like Date and raw binary data, optimized for speed and traversal.

quizQuestions.question: What aggregation stage filters documents so only those matching specified conditions pass through?
quizQuestions.explanation: $match acts like a filter stage, equivalent to the query parameter in find().

quizQuestions.question: When should you embed related data in MongoDB instead of referencing another collection?
options: When data is accessed together frequently and has a bounded 1-to-few relationship
When data grows without limit into millions of records
quizQuestions.explanation: Embedding optimizes read performance when data is bounded and almost always retrieved together.

quizQuestions.question: What method can you append to a MongoDB query to inspect index usage and execution statistics?
quizQuestions.explanation: explain("executionStats") provides detailed metrics on whether an index was scanned or a full collection scan occurred.

quizQuestions.question: What MongoDB operator performs an atomic increment on a numeric field?
quizQuestions.explanation: $inc atomically increments a field by a specified value without requiring a read-modify-write cycle.

quizQuestions.question: In Mongoose ODM, what method replaces an ObjectId reference with the actual populated document?
quizQuestions.explanation: populate() automatically looks up referenced documents from designated collections and injects them.

quizQuestions.question: What is a TTL (Time-To-Live) index used for in MongoDB?
options: Automatically deleting documents after a specified time interval (e.g. sessions, logs)
quizQuestions.explanation: TTL indexes automatically remove expired documents from collections after an elapsed duration.

quizQuestions.question: What is a replica set in MongoDB?
options: A group of mongod instances that maintain the same data set for high availability and failover
A backup hard drive in the cloud
quizQuestions.explanation: Replica sets provide redundancy and high availability with automatic failover in production environments.

quizQuestions.question: Why is storing JWT access tokens in HttpOnly cookies safer against XSS attacks than localStorage?
options: JavaScript code running in the browser cannot read HttpOnly cookies, mitigating token theft via XSS
quizQuestions.explanation: HttpOnly flag blocks client-side JavaScript access to the cookie, protecting it from malicious XSS extraction.

quizQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Stripe Webhooks in a payment flow?
options: Displaying credit card form inputs in React
Receiving asynchronous, cryptographic notifications from Stripe when payment succeeds on their servers
Calculating sales tax on the client
quizQuestions.explanation: Webhooks ensure fulfillment occurs reliably even if the customer closes their browser before redirect.

quizQuestions.question: What is a key advantage of using TanStack Query (React Query) over manual useEffect data fetching?
options: Automatic caching, background refetching, deduping, and loading/error state management
It rewrites backend SQL queries automatically
It eliminates the need for Node.js
It replaces React components with HTML
quizQuestions.explanation: TanStack Query dramatically simplifies server state synchronization, caching, and cache invalidation.

quizQuestions.question: What mechanism prevents Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) when using cookies for API authorization?
options: Using SameSite=Strict/Lax cookie attribute and CSRF tokens
quizQuestions.explanation: SameSite cookie attribute prevents the browser from sending cookies on cross-origin requests, blocking CSRF.

quizQuestions.question: What is the responsibility of a reverse proxy like Nginx in production MERN hosting?
options: SSL/TLS termination, request routing, static file caching, and load balancing
quizQuestions.explanation: Reverse proxies shield Node application servers, handle HTTPS certificates, and serve static assets efficiently.

quizQuestions.question: In a REST API, what should a POST request creating a new resource return as its HTTP status code?
quizQuestions.explanation: 201 Created indicates that the request succeeded and resulted in a new resource being created.

quizQuestions.question: What is CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) enforced by?
quizQuestions.explanation: CORS is a browser security mechanism that restricts HTTP requests initiated from scripts outside the origin.

quizQuestions.question: What command starts a Docker container in detached background mode?
quizQuestions.explanation: The -d flag in docker run runs the container in detached mode in the background.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is an immutable data type in Python?
quizQuestions.explanation: Tuples cannot be altered once created; lists, dictionaries, and sets are all mutable.

quizQuestions.question: What is the output of len([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) in Python?
quizQuestions.explanation: len() returns the number of elements in the collection, which is 5.

quizQuestions.question: What keyword defines a function in Python?
quizQuestions.explanation: In Python, functions are defined using the def keyword followed by the function name and parameters.

quizQuestions.question: What is the correct syntax for a list comprehension squaring all numbers in nums = [1, 2, 3]?
quizQuestions.explanation: [expression for item in iterable] is the standard Python list comprehension syntax.

quizQuestions.question: What does the with statement guarantee when working with file I/O in Python?
options: The file is automatically closed when the block exits even if an exception occurs
The file content is converted to uppercase
The file is saved to the cloud
quizQuestions.explanation: Context managers with the with statement ensure resources like file handles are cleanly closed.

quizQuestions.question: What method is the constructor initialized when creating an instance of a Python class?
quizQuestions.explanation: __init__() is the initializer method automatically invoked upon instantiating a class.

quizQuestions.question: How do you check if a key "email" exists in dictionary user_data in Python?
quizQuestions.explanation: The in keyword performs fast O(1) membership checks on dictionary keys.

quizQuestions.question: Which block in a try-except structure executes only if NO exceptions were raised?
quizQuestions.explanation: The else block in a try statement executes when the try block completes without any exceptions.

quizQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the Java Virtual Machine (JVM)?
options: To compile Java code into C++
To execute Java bytecode instructions on the host platform
quizQuestions.explanation: The JVM provides the cross-platform runtime environment by interpreting and JIT-compiling Java bytecode.

quizQuestions.question: Which keyword prevents a class from being subclassed in Java?
quizQuestions.explanation: Declaring a class final prevents any other class from extending it.

quizQuestions.question: Which collection class implements the List interface with a resizable array backed buffer?
quizQuestions.explanation: ArrayList implements the List interface using a dynamically resizing array for fast O(1) random access.

quizQuestions.question: What is the signature of the entry point method in every standard Java application?
quizQuestions.explanation: public static void main(String[] args) is the required entry point invoked by the JVM.

quizQuestions.question: What is method overloading in Java?
options: Two methods with the same name but different parameter lists within the same class
Subclass replacing a parent method implementation
A method running in multiple threads
quizQuestions.explanation: Overloading allows multiple methods in the same class to share the same name as long as their parameter signatures differ.

quizQuestions.question: Which interface in Java guarantees unique elements without duplicates?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Set interface represents a collection that contains no duplicate elements.

quizQuestions.question: What memory area stores Java objects created with the new keyword?
quizQuestions.explanation: Objects are allocated on the Heap, while local variable references and method call frames live on the Stack.

quizQuestions.question: What does the finally block do in Java exception handling?
options: Executes only when an uncaught error occurs
Executes always, regardless of whether an exception was thrown or caught
Rethrows the exception to the caller
quizQuestions.explanation: The finally block executes unconditionally for crucial cleanup actions like closing database connections or streams.

quizQuestions.question: What operator in C++ is used to get the memory address of a variable?
quizQuestions.explanation: The address-of operator & returns the memory address where the variable is stored.

quizQuestions.question: What happens when dynamic memory allocated with new is never released with delete in C++?
options: A memory leak occurs, consuming heap space until the process terminates
The compiler throws a syntax error
quizQuestions.explanation: Unlike Java or Python, C++ does not have garbage collection; unreleased heap memory leads to memory leaks.

quizQuestions.question: What does RAII stand for in modern C++ engineering?
quizQuestions.explanation: RAII binds the lifecycle of a resource to the lifetime of an object, guaranteeing cleanup upon destruction.

quizQuestions.question: Which smart pointer in modern C++ represents exclusive, non-copyable ownership of a heap resource?
quizQuestions.explanation: std::unique_ptr guarantees that exactly one pointer owns the dynamically allocated object.

quizQuestions.question: What is the average time complexity for searching an element in std::unordered_map in C++?
quizQuestions.explanation: std::unordered_map is implemented with a hash table, offering average O(1) lookup time.

quizQuestions.question: What is the time complexity to insert an element at the end of a std::vector when capacity is sufficient?
quizQuestions.explanation: vector.push_back() runs in amortized O(1) constant time.

quizQuestions.question: In a Binary Search Tree (BST), which traversal visits nodes in non-decreasing sorted order?
quizQuestions.explanation: In-order traversal (Left, Root, Right) processes nodes of a BST in ascending sorted order.

quizQuestions.question: What does the const keyword on a C++ member function indicate (e.g. void display() const)?
options: The method can only be called once
The method guarantees it will not modify any member variables of the object
The method runs in constant O(1) time
quizQuestions.explanation: A const member function cannot modify non-mutable state of the invoking instance.

quizQuestions.question: What is the time complexity of Binary Search on a sorted array of size N?
quizQuestions.explanation: Binary search cuts the remaining search space in half with every iteration, yielding O(log N) runtime.

quizQuestions.question: Which algorithm is optimal for finding the shortest path between nodes in an unweighted graph?
quizQuestions.explanation: BFS explores nodes level by level, ensuring the first time a destination is reached corresponds to the fewest edges.

quizQuestions.question: What two key properties must a problem have to be solvable via Dynamic Programming?
options: Odd number of inputs and prime numbers
quizQuestions.explanation: DP applies when solutions to subproblems can be reused (overlapping) to construct the global optimum (optimal substructure).

quizQuestions.question: What data structure is typically used to implement Breadth-First Search (BFS)?
quizQuestions.explanation: A FIFO (First-In, First-Out) queue processes vertices in exact order of discovery distance.

quizQuestions.question: In Floyd Cycle Detection algorithm (Tortoise and Hare), what are the speeds of the two pointers?
options: Slow moves 1 step, Fast moves 2 steps per turn
Slow moves 2 steps, Fast moves 4 steps
They start at opposite ends of the list
quizQuestions.explanation: The fast pointer advances 2 nodes while the slow pointer advances 1; if a cycle exists, they must meet.

quizQuestions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort when a bad pivot is consistently chosen?
quizQuestions.explanation: If the smallest or largest element is picked every time as pivot on an already sorted array, QuickSort degrades to O(N^2).

quizQuestions.question: What algorithmic paradigm does merge sort use?
quizQuestions.explanation: Merge sort divides the array in halves, recursively sorts each, and then conquers by merging the halves.

quizQuestions.question: What is the maximum number of edges a connected undirected graph with N vertices can have without self-loops or multiple edges?
quizQuestions.explanation: Every vertex can connect to N - 1 other vertices; dividing by 2 accounts for undirected duplicate counts.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary difference between Supervised and Unsupervised Learning?
options: Supervised uses labeled training data with target outputs; Unsupervised learns patterns without labels
Supervised only works on numbers; Unsupervised only works on images
Unsupervised requires GPU clusters while Supervised runs on phones
quizQuestions.explanation: Supervised learning pairs input features with ground-truth target labels; unsupervised learning discovers latent structures in unlabeled data.

quizQuestions.question: What problem occurs when a model performs exceptionally on training data but poorly on unseen test data?
quizQuestions.explanation: Overfitting occurs when a complex model memorizes noise in the training set rather than learning generalizable patterns.

quizQuestions.question: Which metric is best suited for evaluating a fraud detection model with severe class imbalance (99.9% non-fraud)?
quizQuestions.explanation: A naive model predicting non-fraud every time gets 99.9% accuracy; Precision and Recall properly measure detection of the minority positive class.

quizQuestions.question: What regularization technique adds a penalty proportional to the absolute values of the coefficients, driving some weights to exact zero?
quizQuestions.explanation: L1 Lasso encourages sparsity by driving less important feature weights exactly to zero, performing automatic feature selection.

quizQuestions.question: What does PCA (Principal Component Analysis) accomplish?
options: Reduces feature dimensionality while preserving as much data variance as possible
quizQuestions.explanation: PCA projects high-dimensional data onto orthogonal axes that maximize variance, simplifying models.

quizQuestions.question: What optimization algorithm updates model parameters iteratively in the direction of steepest descent of the loss function?
quizQuestions.explanation: Gradient descent computes the gradient of the loss surface with respect to parameters and steps in the opposite direction.

quizQuestions.question: What is the role of an activation function in a neural network?
options: To introduce non-linearity so the network can learn complex arbitrary patterns
quizQuestions.explanation: Without non-linear activation functions (like ReLU), stacking layers would simply collapse to a single linear transformation.

quizQuestions.question: What is the Elbow Method used for in K-Means clustering?
options: Determining the optimal number of clusters K by plotting inertia/distortion
quizQuestions.explanation: The elbow method plots sum of squared errors vs K; the "elbow" point where distortion drop levels off indicates an optimal K.

quizQuestions.question: Why are NumPy arrays substantially faster than standard Python lists for numeric computations?
options: NumPy arrays are stored in contiguous C-style memory blocks with homogeneous types, enabling CPU vectorization
Python lists have a 100-item maximum limit
NumPy deletes all comments in code
quizQuestions.explanation: Contiguous memory layout and single data types allow CPU SIMD instructions to operate without Python object overhead.

quizQuestions.question: In Pandas, what indexer selects data strictly by integer zero-based position?
quizQuestions.explanation: .iloc[] selects rows and columns by integer index positions, whereas .loc[] selects by label.

quizQuestions.question: Which Pandas method fills missing NaN values with a substitute value (such as column mean)?
quizQuestions.explanation: fillna() fills NA/NaN values using the specified value or interpolation method.

quizQuestions.question: What Pandas method groups rows that share values in specified columns to apply aggregate functions?
quizQuestions.explanation: groupby() splits the data into groups based on some criteria, applies a function, and combines results.

quizQuestions.question: What is broadcasting in NumPy?
options: Sending data over WiFi to other computers
How NumPy treats arrays with different shapes during arithmetic operations without copying data
quizQuestions.explanation: Broadcasting allows arithmetic operations between arrays of different shapes according to strict dimension compatibility rules.

quizQuestions.question: What method outputs summary statistics (mean, std, min, max, quartiles) for numeric columns in a DataFrame?
quizQuestions.explanation: df.describe() generates descriptive statistics summarizing the central tendency, dispersion, and shape of a dataset.

quizQuestions.question: Which Seaborn visualization displays distributions across quartiles and highlights outliers?
quizQuestions.explanation: Box plots display median, interquartile range (IQR), and individual outlier points beyond whiskers.

quizQuestions.question: How do you filter a DataFrame df to only rows where column "age" is greater than 25?
quizQuestions.explanation: df[df["age"] > 25] uses boolean indexing to return only rows satisfying the condition.

quizQuestions.question: What is the key difference between WHERE and HAVING clauses in SQL?
options: WHERE filters rows before aggregation; HAVING filters aggregated groups created by GROUP BY
WHERE is for sorting; HAVING is for filtering
quizQuestions.explanation: WHERE filters individual row records before grouping; HAVING filters the aggregated results after GROUP BY.

quizQuestions.question: Which JOIN returns all rows from the left table, and matching rows from the right table (filling NULLs if no match)?
quizQuestions.explanation: LEFT JOIN preserves every record from the left table, matching rows from the right table where possible.

quizQuestions.question: What does a Common Table Expression (CTE) defined with WITH do?
options: Permanently creates a new table on disk
Defines a temporary named result set accessible within the scope of a single query
quizQuestions.explanation: CTEs improve query readability and modularity by creating transient named result sets for subsequent SELECTs.

quizQuestions.question: What window function assigns a sequential unique integer to rows within a partition without gaps?
quizQuestions.explanation: ROW_NUMBER() always assigns a unique incrementing integer (1, 2, 3...) to each row in the partition.

quizQuestions.question: What do the four letters in ACID transaction properties stand for?
quizQuestions.explanation: ACID guarantees that database transactions are processed reliably even in power failure or crash conditions.

quizQuestions.question: What SQL constraint ensures that all values in a column are distinct from one another?
quizQuestions.explanation: The UNIQUE constraint ensures that all values stored in the specified column are distinct.

quizQuestions.question: What is a database index analogous to?
options: A full backup of the server
An index at the back of a textbook that lets you jump straight to relevant pages without reading every page
The cover design of a book
quizQuestions.explanation: Indexes create fast lookup data structures (typically B-Trees) allowing the engine to locate rows without full table scans.

quizQuestions.question: What is the purpose of the LEAD() and LAG() window functions?
options: Accessing data from subsequent (LEAD) or preceding (LAG) rows relative to the current row without a self-join
quizQuestions.explanation: LEAD and LAG access adjacent rows in partition order, perfect for calculating period-over-period growth or differences.

quizQuestions.question: What is the primary benefit of Auto Layout in Figma?
options: It automatically generates backend database schemas
It creates responsive frames and buttons that adapt dynamically to content size and spacing changes
It replaces vector drawings with photos
quizQuestions.explanation: Auto Layout allows frames and components to grow or shrink dynamically as text or contents change, matching flexbox behavior.

quizQuestions.question: What spatial grid spacing is overwhelmingly standard in modern digital product design?
quizQuestions.explanation: The 8pt grid scales gracefully across various screen densities and pixel ratios on modern devices.

quizQuestions.question: What minimum contrast ratio does WCAG AA require for normal body text against its background?
quizQuestions.explanation: WCAG AA requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for normal text (under 18pt) to ensure readability.

quizQuestions.question: In Figma, what feature combines multiple component states (e.g. default, hover, pressed, disabled) into a single container?
quizQuestions.explanation: Component sets organize variants together so designers can switch states with simple dropdowns.

quizQuestions.question: What animation setting in Figma prototyping smoothly interpolates matching layers between two screens?
quizQuestions.explanation: Smart Animate looks for matching layer names between frames and automatically animates position, size, and opacity.

quizQuestions.question: What are Design Tokens in a modern design system?
options: Atomic design decisions stored as variables (colors, spacing, font sizes, radiuses) shared between design and code
Passwords used to access Figma files
quizQuestions.explanation: Design tokens are single sources of truth for styling values, bridging the gap between Figma styles and CSS/Tailwind tokens.

quizQuestions.question: What Figma mode provides developers with CSS code snippets, spacing measurements, and asset exports?
quizQuestions.explanation: Dev Mode gives engineers exact specs, paddings, CSS properties, and downloadable assets.

quizQuestions.question: What is the difference between a wireframe and a mockup?
options: Wireframes are low-fidelity structural outlines; mockups are high-fidelity visual representations with typography and color
Wireframes are for mobile; mockups are for desktop
Wireframes have code; mockups do not
quizQuestions.explanation: Wireframes focus on information hierarchy and structure; mockups focus on aesthetic fidelity and styling.

quizQuestions.question: What are the three main local states that files reside in with Git?
options: Working Directory, Staging Area (Index), and Git Repository (.git)
quizQuestions.explanation: Git tracks changes across the working tree, the staging area (index), and the committed repository object store.

quizQuestions.question: What command stages all modified and newly created files in the current directory?
quizQuestions.explanation: git add . stages all current directory additions and modifications to the index.

quizQuestions.question: What is the crucial difference between git revert and git reset --hard?
options: git revert creates a new commit undoing previous changes safely; git reset --hard wipes commits and discards uncommitted changes
git revert is for branches; git reset is for tags
quizQuestions.explanation: git revert is safe for shared branches because it preserves commit history by appending an inverse commit.

quizQuestions.question: What happens during a Fast-Forward merge in Git?
options: The target branch pointer simply moves forward to the commit tip of the merged branch without creating a merge commit
quizQuestions.explanation: When no diverging commits exist on the base branch, Git simply fast-forwards the pointer.

quizQuestions.question: What file in a Git repository specifies intentionally untracked files to ignore (like node_modules and .env)?
quizQuestions.explanation: .gitignore tells Git which files or directories to ignore when determining untracked changes.

quizQuestions.question: What does git fetch do compared to git pull?
options: git fetch downloads commits and references from the remote without merging them into your current branch
git fetch pushes local commits to GitHub
git fetch only works on Windows
quizQuestions.explanation: git fetch updates remote tracking branches; git pull is essentially git fetch followed by git merge.

quizQuestions.question: What command allows you to pick an individual specific commit from another branch and apply it to your current branch?
quizQuestions.explanation: git cherry-pick <commit-hash> applies the exact patch introduced by that commit onto HEAD.

quizQuestions.question: What does the HEAD pointer represent in Git?
options: The top of the GitHub website
A reference to the currently checked out commit or branch tip
The oldest commit in the repository
quizQuestions.explanation: HEAD points to the currently active branch or commit in your working tree.

quizQuestions.question: What is the most effective approach when writing a freelance proposal to a client?
options: Copy-pasting a generic resume of every tool you know
Focusing immediately on the client specific problem and outlining a concise plan to solve it
Offering to work for free indefinitely
quizQuestions.explanation: Clients hire freelancers who understand their exact pain point and demonstrate a clear path to achieve results.

quizQuestions.question: What is "Scope Creep" in freelance project management?
options: A computer virus infecting freelance software
When a client gradually requests additional features or revisions outside the agreed original scope without extra payment
A freelancer arriving late to a meeting
The price of software subscriptions increasing
quizQuestions.explanation: Scope creep occurs when project boundaries expand beyond the original contract without budget adjustments.

quizQuestions.question: What is value-based pricing?
options: Pricing based on the estimated financial return or impact the project creates for the client rather than hours spent
Giving clients a 50% discount on every invoice
Charging the exact same rate as your competitors
quizQuestions.explanation: Value-based pricing decouples earnings from time by pricing based on the tangible business outcome generated.

quizQuestions.question: What should you ALWAYS require before beginning work on a fixed-price freelance project?
options: A signed contract and an upfront deposit (e.g. 30%-50%) or escrow funding
The client full credit card details
quizQuestions.explanation: An upfront deposit and written agreement protect your time and ensure client commitment.

quizQuestions.question: What is the fastest way to turn one-time clients into predictable monthly income?
options: Offering monthly maintenance, ongoing optimization, or content retainer packages
Refusing to finish the original project
quizQuestions.explanation: Retainer agreements provide steady recurring revenue by continuously supporting the client ongoing needs.

quizQuestions.question: Why is an initial discovery call valuable before quoting a project price?
options: It gives you time to diagnose the real business problem, timeline, and budget constraints
It is required by federal law
To check if the client has a nice microphone
quizQuestions.explanation: Discovery calls uncover nuances that prevent mispriced quotes and set proper mutual expectations.

quizQuestions.question: How should you professionally handle a client request that is clearly outside the signed scope of work?
options: Ignore the client message and disappear
Politely acknowledge the request, explain it is outside the initial scope, and provide a clear quote/timeline to add it
Perform all extra work for free
quizQuestions.explanation: A change order document or quote for the add-on preserves professional relationships while guarding your time.

options: Detailed case studies with real client testimonials and measurable results
A list of your college grades
A photo of your home workspace
quizQuestions.explanation: Case studies showing the before-and-after business impact and client testimonials give social proof and confidence.
